title: Tissue Engineering of a Human 3D in vitro Tumor Test System
protocol: Rinse the vascular system of the porcine jejunal segment via cannulated arterial access and the intestinal lumen with PBS-.
Repeat rinsing until it is completely clean.
Prepare a 200 mm diameter glass tank with 4 adapters and connect them via silicon tubes to the peristaltic pump (Ismatec).
Fill reservoir bottles with decellularization (DZ) solution and check the tubing system for possible air bubbles.
Connect the intestinal lumen with cable ties to the glass connectors for luminal flow.
Pump 500 ml DZ solution into the red arterial access of the vascular system.
Interrupt the pumping process every 15 min to manually press out the entire intestinal lumen.
Monitor and maintain the pressure of the buffer solution between 80 - 100 mm Hg during decellularization.
Wash the BioVaSc with PBS- until it is free of cell remnants ("completely white").
Fill the BioVaSc completely with DZ solution and incubate it submerged in DZ solution overnight at 4 °C on a rocking shaker.
Repeat step 1.6 for thorough washing.
Place the BioVaSc in DNase solution and incubate overnight at 4 °C on a rocking shaker.
Remove DNase solution and rinse with washing buffer.
γ-sterilize the sample with 25 kGy.
Cut skin biopsy into strips of 2 - 3 mm width with scalpel.
Rinse the tissue strips 3 times with PBS solution.
Cover the tissue with Dispase solution and incubate it for 16 - 18 hours at 4 °C.
Separate epidermis from dermis using tweezers and transfer both separately into petri dishes filled with PBS+.
Rinse dermis strips once with Versene.
Add 10 ml of Trypsin/EDTA solution to the dermis strips and incubate it in the incubator for 40 minutes.
Stop the enzyme reaction immediately by adding 1% FCS.
Transfer skin strips to a petri dish filled with VascuLife.
Scratch out each strip with the scalpel 8 times on each side, applying slight pressure.
Transfer the produced cell suspension via a cell strainer into a centrifuge tube and rinse the cell strainer three times with VascuLife.
Centrifuge the tube at 1,200 x g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the cell pellet with VascuLife.
Chop dermis strips into small pieces using the scalpel to isolate fibroblasts.
Add 10 ml of collagenase solution to the chopped dermis pieces and incubate it for 45 minutes in the incubator.
Centrifuge the tissue and carefully remove the supernatant.
Wash the pellet once with DMEM + 10% FCS + PenStrep, then centrifuge again and carefully remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in culture medium and transfer it to a T75 culture flask to allow cells to grow out of the tissue.
Cut the tubular SIS-Muc open on one side and fix it between two metal rings (cell crowns, 10 mm diameter).
Cover the SIS-Muc in cell culture medium overnight.
Seed isolated cells in defined cell numbers on one or both sides of the SIS for mono- or co-culture set-up.
Seed 8,000 cells/cm² of primary mvECs in a total volume of 100 μl onto the basolateral surface of the SIS (former serosa).
Fill the well with medium to ensure a submersed culture after 3 hr.
Allow endothelial cells to adhere for 3 days.
Flip the static culture system by 180° and transfer it to a 12-well plate.
Seed a mixture of primary dermal fibroblasts (8,000 cells/cm²) and tumor cells (15,000 cells/cm²) within a total volume of 500 μl on the apical surface of the SIS (the side of the former lumen).
Allow cells to adhere for 3 hr.
Fill the well with medium (submersed culture, medium: 50% Vasculife + 50% DMEM supplemented with 10% FCS).
Culture the tumor test system under static conditions at 37 °C, 5% CO2 in an incubator for additional 14 days.
Change culture medium every 2 - 3 days.
Fix the SIS-Muc between two metal rings and seed primary mvECs as described.
Remove the SIS-Muc from the metal rings after 3 days and insert it into the flow reactor.
Apply primary dermal fibroblasts and tumor cells onto the matrix in the bioreactor using a syringe and cannula.
Allow the cells to adhere for 3 hr before filling the bioreactor system with culture medium.
Initiate dynamic culture conditions with constant medium flow (3.8 ml/min, 37 °C, and 5% CO2) on the following day.
Maintain the dynamic culture for 14 days.
Change the culture medium after 7 days during dynamic culture.
Remove the culture medium from the seeded collagenous matrix.
Fix the tissue with 4% paraformaldehyde for 2 hr.
Transfer the SIS from the metal insert to a tissue embedding cassette.
Dehydrate the tissue for paraffin infiltration.
Cut the SIS in 2-3 slices.
Place cut SIS slices in a paraffin-filled metal base mold, with the cut surfaces facing downwards.
Add tissue cassette on top of the mold as backing.
Cut 5 μm slices and float them on a 40 °C water bath for straightening.
Mount slides onto suitable glass slides.
Use uncoated slides for H&E stains and polylysine-coated slides for immunohistological staining to improve attachment.
Let slices dry thoroughly.
Melt paraffin, remove with xylene and rehydrate slices for staining.
Deparaffinize and rehydrated slides are placed in a steam cooker with heated citrate buffer (pH 6.0) for antigen retrieval.
Transfer slides to washing buffer (0.5 M TBS buffer + 0.5% Tween).
Circle slices with PAP pen to minimize the required volume for staining solutions.
Place the slide in a moisture chamber.
Apply primary antibody dilutions to the slices and incubate for 1 hr at RT.
Carefully wash off primary antibodies with washing buffer.
Use Ultra Vision Quanto Detection System HRP DAB (Thermo Scientific) according to the recommended protocol.
Counterstain nuclei with Hematoxylin for 1 minute.
Mount slides with an aqueous medium.
Dry mounted slides.
Image slides using an inverse microscope.
